svg.title: What a reasoning model returns: hidden, summarized, carried over, and answered
svg.desc: A reasoning model produces four things. The raw reasoning tokens are never returned by OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google, but they are billed as output tokens. A reasoning summary is optional: OpenAI returns it when reasoning.summary is set, Anthropic returns summarized thinking with display set to summarized, and Google returns thought summaries when they are enabled; a summary is written for people and is not the model's actual reasoning. Opaque carry-over items, OpenAI reasoning items with encrypted content, Anthropic thinking blocks with a signature, and Google thought signatures, must be sent back unchanged on the next turn of a tool loop. The final answer is what you grade, with code and evaluation sets. A note says that faithfulness research found reasoning text often omits what actually influenced the answer, so judge outcomes, not the story. Grade the answer, budget for the hidden tokens, and pass the opaque parts back untouched.

g.text: What a reasoning model gives you back, and what to do with each part
Never returned by OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google
Still billed as output tokens and still counted against the output limit
OpenAI reasoning.summary; Anthropic display "summarized"; Google thought summaries
Written for people: useful for debugging, not the model's actual reasoning
OpenAI encrypted reasoning items; Anthropic thinking signatures; Google thought signatures
Send back unchanged on the next turn of a tool loop; never edit or drop them
The text or structured result your feature uses
Grade this: rules checked by code, quality measured on an evaluation set
Faithfulness research found that reasoning text often leaves out what actually influenced the answer: judge outcomes, not the story.
Grade the answer, budget for the hidden tokens, and pass the opaque parts back untouched.
